title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 43–45). Grothendieck is setting up the combinatorics that index the boundary ('structure à l'infini') of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}. He uses 'MD-graphes' (Mumford–Deligne graphs), i.e. stable graphs.

Graphs and contractions. A graph G has vertex set S, edge set A, and half-edges or 'arcs' Ã with involution σ. A generalized morphism G' → G may contract some edges to points. For a set C' ⊂ A' of edges, the quotient G'/C' is the pushout (amalgamated sum) that collapses each connected component of the subgraph (S', C') to a single vertex.

Factorization (55). On this page he states that every generalized morphism f: G' → G factors uniquely (up to unique isomorphism) as G' → G_0 → G. The first map is the quotient by the set C' of edges contracted by f. The second map is an ordinary graph morphism.

Transport of stable-graph structure. Suppose G' is finite and comes from an MD-graph \underline{G}'. The extra data are a set of legs (marked points) I' → S' and a genus function g': S' → ℕ. Let G = G'/C', with vertex set S. For α ∈ S, let G'(α) be the connected subgraph of (S', C') that is collapsed to α, with vertex set S'_α. Define:
- the legs I := I', mapped to S by the composite I' → S' → S;
- the genus (56): g_α = Σ_{α' ∈ S'_α} g'_{α'} + h^1(G'(α)).
Here h^1 = #edges − #vertices + 1 is the first Betti number of the connected graph G'(α).

This is exactly the genus of the curve obtained by smoothing all nodes inside the component: arithmetic genus = sum of the geometric genera of the components plus the number of independent cycles of the dual graph.

The next page checks that \underline{G} is again MD (stable). Connectedness is inherited. The stability inequality 2g_α + n_α ≥ 3 is derived from the fact that the vertex type (g_α, ν̂_α) is the modular type of the stable sub-MD-graph \underline{G}(α), whose legs are I'_α ⊔ B̃'_α.

Purpose. This makes 'stable graphs with contractions' a category (a poset of types up to isomorphism). That category indexes the stratification of the DM boundary and its specialization relations: contracting edges corresponds to smoothing nodes, i.e. passing to a larger (less degenerate) stratum.
errors: No mathematical error. The formula (56) is correct, provided G'(α) is understood as the connected component of the subgraph (S', C') collapsed to α, so that h^1 = |C'_α| − |S'_α| + 1. Loops and multiple edges are correctly accounted for by h^1.

The factorization in (55) is unique only up to unique isomorphism of the intermediate graph G_0. Note also that G_0 here is the quotient graph, not the subgraph G'_0 of the previous page (overloaded notation).
The transcription's '(par l'une des arêtes ...)' would be mathematically wrong: the quotient is by ALL edges contracted by f. The handwriting is more plausibly 'par l'ens. des arêtes'.

ideas.what: Category of graphs with generalized morphisms (edge contractions), and the unique factorization of any generalized morphism into a contraction followed by an ordinary graph morphism
ideas.modern_name: Category of stable graphs with contractions/isomorphisms (graph category underlying modular operads); a contraction–morphism factorization system
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne–Mumford/Knudsen boundary stratification; formalized by Behrend–Manin (1995/96), Getzler–Kapranov (Modular operads, 1998), Borisov–Manin, Costello
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' / Teichmüller tower and stable curves

ideas.what: Contraction of a stable (MD) graph, with genus rule g_α = Σ g'_{α'} + h^1(G'(α)) and legs transported
ideas.modern_name: Edge contraction of stable graphs / specialization of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983, Kontsevich 1992–94, Getzler–Kapranov 1998, Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but entirely standard definition: contraction of stable graphs with the genus formula via first Betti number, plus the contraction/ordinary-morphism factorization. It is of historical interest as an early, self-made formalization of stable-graph combinatorics (likely early 1980s, before Behrend–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov). It contains nothing a specialist today would find new.
transcription_corrections: '(par l'une des arêtes de G' contractées par f, justement)' should likely read '(par l'ens. des arêtes de G' contractées par f, justement)'.
The marginal note under the sum in (56) reads 'α' ∈ S'_α ‖ Sommets de G'(α)', i.e. S'_α = set of vertices of G'(α).
Page number in the margin: 44; folio '22' on the next page.
